full_judgment: 2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that 5 kathas of land equivalent to more or less .8 decimal of mouza Khojarbagh, being Plot No. 3/1)/A, 1st Colony Mirpur, R.S. Plot No. 109, R.S. Khatian No. 33,.P.S. Mirpur, Dhaka was allotted to Md. Jamiruddin by a deed of settlement dated 27.07.1953 by ..the , then Government of East Pakistan; that said Md. Jamiruddin constructed a semi-puma house on his allotted land and resided therein with his family members; that he paid rents and taxes of the Union Parishad and after 12 years of his possession, he on 01.06.1968 applied to the concerned authority for issuing clearance certificate to construct a two storied building as per approved plan of the DIT and that the authority issued clearance certificate on 21.07.1968; that said Md. Jamiruddin while had been owning and possessing the suit property, he being in need of cash money proposed to sell the suit property to the plaintiffs on the 1st week of March, 1971 and the plaintiffs agreed to purchase the same at a consideration money of TK. 40,000.00; that on 12.03.1971 said Md. Jamiruddin on receipt of TK.20,000.00 from the plaintiffs executed a bainapatra with plaintiff No. 1 in favour of both the plaintiffs; that as per stipulation of the said bainapatra, the sale deed was required to be completed within 3 years from the date of bainapatra; that Jamiruddin died on 13.04.1973 at 4:00 P.M. leaving behind his only son Nasiruddin as heir and that he was buried at the grave year of Section 10, Mirpur on 13.-4.1973 at 3:00 RM.; that while Nasiruddin had been owning and possessing the suit property he admitted the liability of his late father under the said bainapatra as he was an attesting witness of the same; that thereafter, on several occasions he received part of the balance consideration money from the plaintiffs by putting his signature on the back page of the said bainapatra; that on 13.04.1985 Nasiruddin executed. and registered the sale deed being No. 1191 in favour of the plaintiffs on receipt of the rest balance consideration money of 'TK. 11,500:00 and delivered physical possession of the suit property to the petitioners; that Nasiruddin is a Bangladeshi National and permanent citizen of Bangladesh and that he never opted for Pakistan; that Nasiruddin obtained a succession certificate from the 3rd Court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka vide Succession Certificate Case No. 1011 of 1984; that the plaintiffs while were in ownership and possession of the suit property since their purchase on 13.04.1985 peacefully and uninterruptedly, the defendant No. 1 with a group of his men forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs on 15.04.1986 at 3:00 P.M. from the suit property on the plea that the defendant No. 1 purchased the suit property from one Rahim Baksh on 28.091.1977 through sale deed being No. 27959 who alleged to have purchased the same from Md. Jamiruddin by a sale deed being No.1407 dated 23.04.1975; that Md. Jamiruddin never sold the suit property to said Rahim Baksh and that Rahim Baksh never owned and possessed the suit property; that the deed of sale alleged to have been executed and registered by Rahim Baksh is a forge and fabricated documents; that defendant No. 1 has not acquired any right, title and interest in the suit property on the basis of the said deed; that the plaintiffs acquired valid right, title and interest in the suit property by purchase from the lawful owner.
